signals.text: From our Leadership and Lifeskills course, to 1:1 progress conversations with their tutors, personalised learning programmes and clear careers advice, we continually strive to go above and beyond, to give our senior students the tools and resources they need to flourish at GCSE and beyond.
Mountain Biking, Sailing, Windsurfing and Water Polo are among many alternative options which enable our pupils to challenge themselves and experience success in an alternative to team fixtures.

Many students opt to continue their journey and study English at A-level: as an academic subject, it develops your ability to think, reason, and communicate, which, in turn, helps you access your other subjects and shapes the adult you will become.
Following Options Evening, students can discuss their GCSE options with their Form T utor, Head of Y ear, and their allocated senior staff member.

DT GCSE Grade Structure & Assessment Methods Since 2017, a numerical grading system from 9 to 1 has been introduced, replacing the traditional letter grades, with 9 being the highest and 1 being the lowest.

Open Morning
SATURDAY 3 OCTOBER
Please join us for our Whole School Open Morning on Saturday 3 October 2026, 9am-11.30am
Nestled in the beautifully picturesque Weald of Kent and only an hour from London, Dulwich Cranbrook is an independent day & boarding school for girls and boys aged 2 to 16 years.
We’ve taken a forward thinking approach to the individual care, encouragement, inspiration and future success of every single child since 1939.
Tumble turners
Our pride
Please take a good look around and perhaps take some time to read why our head, Sophie Bradshaw – is proud to play a part in the history of Dulwich Cranbrook.
Curiosity
Our school life
Our school life grows as our pupils grow, starting from Early Years in Nash House, to Years 1–6 in Prep (in both Little Stream and Upper Prep building) and on to Years 7–11 in Senior School.
Good spirits
Our work
We work hard to make hard work feel like fun, inspiring interest and encouragement so that Maths becomes magical, Science become sensational and English becomes… well, you get the idea.
Originals
Our play
The swish of a brush, the beat of a drum, the clack of a bat or the glide of a dive… our children enjoy the freedom to explore a wide and wonderous variety of co-curricular options.
Scoffers
Our stories
With so many interesting things going on in our school, there’s always lots to tell you about – so why not stay up-to-date by keeping your finger on the pulse and your ear to the ground.
Role models
Join... our family
If your family would like to become part of our family, please take a little time to look through our admissions process – and we hope to meet you for a tour very soon.
Seekers
Our Explorers
Our free Little Explorers parent and toddler group is the perfect way to introduce your family to the wonderful world of Dulwich Cranbrook.

SATURDAY 3 OCTOBER
Please join us for our Whole School Open Morning on Saturday 3 October 2026, 9am-11.30am
Little Explorers
A Curiosity of Seekers
Our Parent & Toddler Group, ‘Little Explorers’, is held every Monday & Friday during term time, from 9.00 – 10.00am in the Nash House Hall.
This is a wonderful way of seeing Nash House in action, getting to know our lovely Early Years teachers and meeting other families. This term we will be holding French Yoga sessions. Designed for children aged 18 months – 4 years and their parents, sessions involve Exploring and observing seasonal changes with our early years staff, making dens, creating potions and other delights in the mud kitchen, being introduced to child safe tools, toasting bread over the fire, mud sledging, natural art, identifying and naming flora and fauna. Warming up with a hot chocolate by the fire when the weather turns, story time around the fire, learning how to dress for weather and keep themselves safe.
Mondays 10.00-11.00am: Outdoor Explorers
Explore and observe seasonal changes with our Early Years team. Make dens, create potions and other delights in the mud kitchen, learn to use child-safe tools, toast bread over the fire, go mud sledging, and create natural art. Discover the flora and fauna around us, enjoy stories and hot chocolate around the fire, and learn how to dress for the weather and stay safe outdoors.
Fridays 9.00-10.00am: Music & Sensory
Getting creative singing songs and rhymes with our early years team and specialist music teacher. Have the chance to explore sensory trays and craft activities together.
Enjoy one free taster session, then £5 per child per session. There is no need to be registered with us, however, it would be ideal if you could let us know if you would like to come so we can make sure we have enough refreshments!
For more information or to let us know that you would like to attend a session, please email nhoffice@dulwichcranbrook.org or call 01580 713043.

Inspection Reports
A compliment of assessors
Please take a moment to review our Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI) reports, of which we are very, very proud.
We are delighted to be able to share our latest ISI report, following an inspection in January 2026. The full ISI report and highlights of the report are available below.
Like all UK independent schools, Dulwich Cranbrook is inspected regularly by the ISI to ensure that high standards are maintained.
The inspection framework introduced in September 2023 marks a notable shift from the previous approach. Under this revised model, ISI no longer uses single-word judgements such as ‘excellent’. Instead, schools are evaluated on whether they have ‘met’ or ‘not met’ the required standards across five key areas.
The inspection confirmed that Dulwich Cranbrook has met all required standards, and the report recognises the School’s “inclusive educational philosophy where children and pupils are valued and known as individuals.”

Drama
A delight of dreamers
Our Head of Drama, Mrs Carter, inspires in our pupils a level of exploration which takes them beyond the classroom and equips them for the challenges of performance – not only for the stage but also for life.
Multiple styles and techniques are taught with a backdrop of enjoyment and collaboration. Children are encouraged to think outside the box, interact with the audience and develop useful skills for a range of scenarios.
Every year group from Nursery upwards performs an annual play or musical, facilitated by three dedicated performance spaces across the school. We also offer LAMDA exams as part of the curriculum for all children in Years 5 to 8, and as an optional extra for Years 9-11. Trips and workshops happen throughout the year including, most recently, Macbeth at the Globe and Hamilton in the West End.
I felt compelled to write to you following last night's Year 6 performance. It was truly astonishing! Everyone involved in the production should be congratulated for delivering such a first-class performance.

Music
A chorus of composers
All children benefit from specialist Music teaching from Nursery upwards.
Music at Dulwich focuses on the joy of performance, the skills that help build individuality and confidence, and the importance of working together as a team. Our teachers believe that Music is for all and this inclusive approach through performance, and particularly singing, has the power to transform and enhance lives. There exists a natural synergy between music and wellbeing, and this empowering approach to Music can be witnessed by the Dulwich community at regular concerts and performances.
Whether it’s Rock School at lunch with six bands jamming away, or the ‘Jigs and Reels’ club providing toe-tapping folk music with joy and confidence – there is always music being played at Dulwich. We provide a wide range of musical groups; choirs from Year 1; string groups from Year 3; jazz, brass, flute, orchestra from Year 5; senior strings and chamber choirs from Year 7.
Sixty percent of pupils from Year 2 upwards learn instruments with termly informal concerts from Year 3. Year 4 is lucky enough to embark on the annual trip to the O2 with Young Voices, and those in the Upper Prep and Senior School perform in our Summer and Winter concerts. Music is at the heart of Dulwich and this spirit is encapsulated with the whole school, including staff, coming together annually for the ‘Big Sing’.
Just one performance has given her such confidence; last night she told me she now feels as though she can achieve anything!

Our governors
An astuteness of navigators
The Dulwich School Cranbrook is a charity, run by a Board of Governors who are trustees.
The School, together with Dulwich Prep and Senior London, is a subsidiary of Dulwich Preparatory Schools Trust. Alongside the Head and Senior Leadership Team, the governors are responsible for setting the overall direction and values of the School and for overseeing and approving the strategic plans and relevant policies. The governors meet as a board at least once a term.
All governors can be contacted by email at bursar@dulwichcranbrook.org or in writing, addressed to the school.
The school’s registered address is: Dulwich Cranbrook, Coursehorn, Cranbrook, Kent TN17 3NP
Board of governors
Robin is a chartered accountant, qualifying with KPMG, with over 40 years of private equity, banking and broader financial experience.
He has recently finished a 10 year term as Chair of Malvern College, an independent school based in Worcestershire, and has been Chair and non-executive director of a number of quoted and unquoted companies in the fund management, media and leisure sectors.
Robin lives locally and all three of his children were pupils at the School.
Now retired, Tom qualified as a chartered accountant before a career in the City of London advising listed companies in the property, financial services and asset management sectors.
Before joining the board of governors in 2022, Tom held a similar position at Radley College for 12 years. He is married with three daughters, who were all educated at the school.
After completing a law degree, James served for 8 years in the Army before moving into executive recruitment. He has worked with clients at Board level for 30 years.
Sonja has been a School Counsellor for two decades, having qualified as a Family Therapist and worked in the private sector within mental health hospitals.
A brand consultant with over 30 years’ experience working across multiple sectors including education. Previously a Governor at another school, Nikki is also a past parent.
Phil is Deputy Head (Academic) of a girls’ independent HMC 11–18 day school in central London and a Team Inspector for the Independent Schools Inspectorate. He has held senior leadership roles as Head of Senior School, Deputy Head (Academic) and Head of Sixth Form.
He has also been Head of Educational Partnerships and Projects for a group of independent girls’ day schools. Phil spent a year as a Senior School Consultant at Dulwich Cranbrook to assist with the transition to being a Senior School.
Now a transformational coach to corporates and individuals, Matt started in education and social care before switching careers. He worked in the banking industry for 24 years and is also a past parent.
Diana Murdoch has had a career across many aspects of education, as a teacher in independent, maintained and special schools, and in research and teaching in the School of Education at the University of Edinburgh. Her current work is an advisory and research role with educational policy makers in European countries. Diana has a PhD in Inclusive Education, a Diploma in Education and an MA in French and History. She has close familial links to the school, attended Little Stream as a child, and is a parent of both a former pupil and gap year student.
Dale Spencer has over 20 years’ experience in the independent school sector working with EYFS, Key Stage 1,2 and 3. He has held a wide range of senior and specialist roles, including Deputy Head, DSL, Head of Boarding and Director of Sport.

Curriculum
A paradigm of problem solvers
We champion an individualised approach to learning – inspiring and supporting each and every child to fulfil their potential, and equipping them with the skills and confidence they need to steer their own unique educational pathway.
We don’t know what careers will even exist by the time our youngest children are ready to choose their own. That’s why we adopt a ‘future-ready’ approach to education – focused on equipping young people with the skills, confidence, and independence they’ll need to steer their own path. We do this by inspiring a love of learning and an open mind.
We operate small classes, with a maximum of 20 children per class. And the majority of our subjects are taught by specialist teachers, in dedicated, purpose-built facilities. As much as possible, we look to bring academic and creative subjects together to enrich the curriculum and appeal to children’s natural curiosity.

Clubs
A hive of busy bees
Dulwich Cranbrook’s extensive clubs offer enables every pupil to do more of what they love and stretch themselves beyond the curriculum.
Clubs take place before and after school or during break times, and we offer a fresh choice each term. Nearly all of our clubs are included in our fees so there are no hidden extras. Where there is interest in a club that we don’t have an in-house specialist for, like Fencing, then we find one – and these clubs are the only ones which carry a charge.

Little Stream Clubs Years 3–4

Some of our current favourites are Rubik’s Cube, Model Railway, Cheerleading and Photography.
I was so excited to find out that there was a Rubik's Cube Club in Upper Prep. I had learnt to solve the cube at home and I met the Year 9 who runs our club when I visited boarding in Year 4. My personal best is 35 seconds and in Rubik's Cube Club, I am also working on learning how to teach new members the basics.
No One Size Fits All
Importantly, the ethos of Dulwich is such that, as our children become teens, they do not have to hide any part of themselves to fit in. They combine being on the Football team with being on the Chess team and they don’t stop singing in the choir, worried that their friends won’t think it is cool. Taking part is celebrated.

Senior School (Year 7+)
A fancy of flourishers
A very warm welcome to our Senior School at Dulwich Cranbrook, where we continue to champion the individual on their academic journey. Offering students the chance to stay at Dulwich for this crucial stage in their education is an incredibly exciting venture. Indeed, our new Senior School facilities have been designed with this in mind.
Our most senior students reside in the specifically designed Coursehorn Building – complete with purpose-built spaces aimed at expanding horizons, with plenty of room for independent study, and access to a beautifully manicured Manor Lawn and Rose Garden.
At the heart of our new Coursehorn Building sits The Henley Café, which opens out onto dedicated outdoor spaces. This space reflects the growing maturity of our most senior students, who are trusted to manage their time effectively as they prepare for their GCSEs.
Our Senior School students benefit from an exceptionally supportive structure around their physical, mental and educational wellbeing. From our Leadership and Lifeskills course, to 1:1 progress conversations with their tutors, personalised learning programmes and clear careers advice, we continually strive to go above and beyond, to give our senior students the tools and resources they need to flourish at GCSE and beyond.
We are committed to creating a supportive yet ambitious environment for our students. In addition, we believe in the importance of open dialogue and communication with parents as their child’s academic journey progresses.
Our class sizes are consistently small to ensure all children are empowered to receive the support they need within the classroom and additional support as required. In addition to academic success, we boast an expansive co-curricular provision which goes beyond Art, Music, Sport and Drama, to also include CCF, Duke of Edinburgh, water sports at Bewl Water and fencing, to name but a few.
Dulwich Cranbrook is an incredibly welcoming community, where every child is supported to achieve their potential. Tours are available all year round – please come and see first-hand how we could be the right fit for your child.

Reviews & awards
A fulfilment of talents
Of course, we think our school is exceptional. But don’t just take our word for it. Here are the thoughts of specialist independent school reviewers and our parents.
Independent reviews
The Good Schools Guide Talk Education Muddy Stilettos
What our parents say
“Thank you for the most amazing 6 years at Dulwich, the school and staff have brought the best out of our daughter. She has gone from a very shy, quiet girl with low self-esteem to one that has confidence and has found skills that she can shine in. We will miss Dulwich a great deal and we are more than certain that without her time at the school we would not have the daughter we have today. We are more than grateful.”
“We have seen both of our children flourish and gain confidence at Dulwich which has been wonderful to see, and now they are ready for a bigger world.”
“The school is excellent on so many levels. Nash House gives such a solid foundation for the building of life skills; and there is such tailoring to each child’s ability that it falls into place so naturally. The teachers in Nursery and Reception are utterly brilliant; kind, warm, caring and bring out the best in each and every child. Talk Education Top 250
We are delighted to have been included in Talk Education’s Top 250 Schools in the UK – not just once but twice! Dulwich Cranbrook Prep School and Senior School have been separately listed in Talk Education’s Top 250 Schools in the UK. Talk Education take into account everything from the quantifiable (results, facilities, destinations and more) to the unquantifiables like word-of-mouth reputation. Not many schools in Kent made the cut, so we are giving ourselves a well-deserved pat on the back! A huge thank you to our pupils, parents and staff for everything you do to make our school community so special.
Performing and Creative Arts Award 2025
We are thrilled to have been shortlisted in the Performing and Creative Arts category of the Talk Education Awards. Our entry focused on the integration of LAMDA (London Academy of Music & Dramatic Art) examinations into the Drama curriculum for pupils in Years 5–8, which is usually offered as an extra-curricular activity. Allocating dedicated lesson time for LAMDA exam preparation ensures that every pupil has the support to become more confident in public speaking and performing. In the Summer Term, we were proud that every Year 5 pupil achieved a distinction!
Muddy Stilettos Award 2025
We are delighted to share that we have been Highly Commended in the Muddy Stilettos Best Schools Awards ‘Inventive Extra-curricular Programme’ category for 2025. This commendation is for our fantastic Year 4 enterprise project. This year, in partnership with Loddington Farm, the children have learnt how apples are grown, pruned, cultivated, pressed and bottled. The children picked apples from our School grounds to create their very own Dulwich apple juice! They are currently in the marketing and sales phase of the project which includes designing labels for their bottles. The apple juice will be sold later in the Summer Term, with all proceeds donated to charity.
Muddy Stilettos Award 2024
We are delighted to have been Highly Commended in the Muddy Stilettos School Awards 2024 ‘Passionate About Sport’ category. Whilst the vast majority of our pupils love and excel at competitive sports, it is not for everyone, and the need for an active alternative became apparent. Recognising that pupils have other strengths and interests, we launched the Dulwich Inspires! programme in 2017. Since then, it has been developed and fine-tuned year on year to become an extra-curricular programme that ignites passion, inspires curiosity, and acts as a catalyst for pupils to discover the depths of their potential. We are incredibly proud of our Dulwich Inspires! programme and it is due to its success that we have been Highly Commended in this category.
Wilder Kent Awards
We are delighted to announce that Dulwich Cranbrook has been awarded a silver award at the Wilder Kent Awards 2023.
As a school and community, we are committed to protecting wildlife. From outdoor education days with the Kent Wildlife Trust, to foraging workshops across our school grounds which enable our children to learn about biodiversity, we strive to maintain and share conscious positive behaviours towards the environment.

Super-curricular
A plethora of possibilities
Alongside Music, Drama, Sport, Art and an array of clubs to spark new interests, we also offer our older students a chance to take part in co-curricular activities which link to academic subjects or career options.
It is these super-curricular activities that our students will reference in university applications, CVs and job interviews in the future.
Real-World Ready
As our pupils move towards GCSE, we offer them more experiences to ready them for the world beyond Dulwich Cranbrook. This includes preparing them for the more independent nature of A-level and university study, introducing them to the enormous choice in the world of work and wider society
Our Year 9 induction trip has a careers focus. Previous trips to the Science Museum as well as touring and working in Formula One’s Digital Broadcast Studio. The trip aims to link their school-based learning across subjects to the world of work.
Popular clubs
Some of our most popular super-curricular clubs are Dulwich GT, Coding and Mock Trial Society.
Our Dulwich Greenpower Team includes engineers, designers, website architects, and fundraisers. Their aim is to design, build and race an electric car. Look out for their workshop next to the playing fields.
Coding club is for those who enjoy their Computer Science lessons and want to take their coding to the next level.
Mock Trial Society is the perfect club for any budding lawyers. The pupils take on the roles of prosecution, defence and magistrate to create a full mock criminal trial. Each trial is based on a real criminal case and take several weeks to research and prepare.

Our care
A kinship of kindness
The development and wellbeing of your children is our top priority. By working closely with parents, we ensure every child gets the individual support they need to flourish.
Dulwich Cranbrook offers outstanding learning support and pastoral care – creating a nurturing environment with a strong focus on personal development.
A collaborative approach
The academic progress and pastoral welfare of every child is closely monitored by their Form Teacher and Head of Year.
Throughout each term, parents will have plenty of opportunities to meet with them to discuss their child’s academic and personal development.
This ongoing dialogue means we see the whole picture at school, just as parents do at home.
Learning support & academic mentoring
We understand that children learn in many different ways. That’s why we take the time to understand each and every child within our care, ensuring they’re given the support they need to develop.
This universal approach to learning support and academic mentoring means that no child is left to fall behind.
And where additional support needs are identified, our Learning Support Team apply targeted interventions early on, providing appropriate provision and reasonable adjustments at every stage of learning and development.
Learning support & academic development brochure download
Pastoral care
Pastoral care is deeply ingrained within our culture and organisational structure. We hold weekly pastoral meetings, so that any concerns that Subject Teachers, Form Tutors or Heads of Year have been supporting children with, can be shared with the wider team. This means that our children receive consistent empathy and support as they move from classroom to sports field to theatre.
Our iSpace Wellbeing Programme is embedded within the curriculum, equipping children with the skills and language they need talk about and manage their feelings. And we ensure students have a number of trusted people they can talk to.
In addition to their teachers, children can talk to our medical staff, their ‘buddy’ or ‘mentor’ from within the student body, or our on-site counsellors from the youth mental health charity Place2Be.
School Aims
Our aim is to inspire and develop confident, capable and compassionate young people – the changemakers of the future.
At Dulwich Cranbrook we are:
Like our pioneering founders, we challenge the norm with original ideas, forward thinking and a fresh approach.
We’re nurturing, inclusive, kind and supportive – we ensure that we understand the unique needs and wellbeing of each and every family.
We encourage our children to explore and enjoy a wide variety of incredible experiences and opportunities.
Enquiring minds and creative imaginations are developed alongside the pride and power of teamwork, to build confidence and character.
Whichever path they choose, we offer a wonderfully well-rounded education to ensure that each child has the skills and confidence to navigate their own educational journey.
